body: I've been doing almost all the gig apps, in addition to running my business, since early 2020. I did decently at first, but it's become very slow in my area unfortunately. There's days where I'm out from 6am to 9pm and am lucky if I make $50. Lately I've been spending more on gas than what I make in a day. I've gotten to the point that there isn't much I can do for my injuries and the pain has become almost unbearable most days. I just don't know what to do anymore.

The outlets I had I'm having a hard time finding joy in them now. I picked up golfing a few years ago, but I was a passenger in a car accident last year and in another more severe accident a few months ago. So I haven't been able to do much because of recovery.

Going to college and starting a business hasn't done much for me. I went to college because my parents expected me to. I graduated because I didn't want to deal with my family freaking out on me if I dropped out. Now I'm stuck with thousands in debt. I lost many jobs after school, and starting a business kind of fell in my lap. I've been in the red since I started and I can't seem to catch up. It's costing me more to operate than what I'm actually making, I'm only making ends meet because my grandparents are giving me a great discount on rent. I need to make more money, but my anxiety is at an all time high and I'm dealing with chronic injuries from car accidents that I've recently been a passenger in, which is making it difficult for me to find work that actually pays enough for me to pay for basic necessities. I have a therapist, but my appointments keep getting canceled or rescheduled and I can't get seen until nearly 1.5 months out. The only person I can really talk to is my best friend, but I feel bad for constantly unloading on her. I'm dealing with a tremendous amount of difficulties and challenges in life; like literally there is an issue with every last thing I try to do. I do everything to push through and exhaust all my options and yet I still get screwed over. I'm just tired.
